_comment: Band C: ranks 161-300 of `just lexicon-candidates` once stopwords are removed, anchored on 'back' as the first entry. Terms already decided in core.json ('damage counter', 'retreat') fall inside the band and are deliberately left to that file rather than duplicated here. See .claude/skills/build-lexicon/SKILL.md.

terms.gloss: Which way up a card or token sits. Face up is open to inspection; face down hides it, and flipping one to face down is how a spent once-per-game allowance is recorded.
terms.glyph_note: Conflates face up and face down, which are opposite states. Splitting them needs the phrase-edge stop rule changed first, since extract() cannot propose 'face down'.

terms.gloss: Carry a card effect or Ability through to completion rather than stopping partway.
A token kept with a card to record something the card itself cannot show, such as a Burn marker or a spent GX or VSTAR allowance.
Shorthand for a damage counter: the marker placed on a Pokemon to record damage, one per 10 points.
A Pokemon card playable straight from hand with nothing beneath it, and the only kind that can start a game in play.
The single Pokemon in front of a player that attacks, takes attacks and must be replaced from the Bench when it leaves.
The face-up zone holding cards a player has used or lost, open for either player to inspect at any time.
The card type attached to a Pokemon to pay attack and retreat costs.
The name printed on a card. Deck-building copy limits and Evolution both work by name rather than by card.
The Energy a card demands before something happens, printed as symbols for an attack and as Retreat Cost for retreating.
The damage a Pokemon can absorb before it is Knocked Out, printed at the top right of the card.
A special printed effect that is neither an ordinary attack nor an Ability, such as a VSTAR Power usable once across the whole game.
A Trainer card subtype played for a one-off effect and then discarded.
A Pokemon Tool: a Trainer card subtype that stays attached to a Pokemon and keeps working while it is there.
An Item card played as a Basic Pokemon, which the Pokemon printed as its origin can later evolve from.
Put an Energy or Tool card onto a Pokemon so it stays there and counts toward what that Pokemon can do.
Put damage counters or a card into a zone directly, without the step that would normally produce it.
Toss a coin, or turn a marker over, to settle an outcome the rules leave to chance or to record that an allowance is spent.
A Special Condition that adds damage counters every Checkup until a coin flip clears it.
A Special Condition that adds damage counters to the affected Pokemon at every Checkup until something removes it.
The size of a Prize Card penalty: Double takes two prizes off the opponent's requirement, against Quadruple's four. Dropping the word makes the two penalties indistinguishable.
A penalty ending the whole match rather than one game, recorded as a loss for the match it attaches to.
The score a match result is worth, which added up over the rounds gives a competitor's standing.
The infraction category for mistakes made inside an active game, as opposed to procedural slips around it.
Lowering a penalty below the guide's starting recommendation because of the circumstances.
The paper a pairing's result is written on and signed before competitors leave the play area.
The submitted roster of a video-game competitor's team, which is the source of truth when it and the in-game team disagree.
The number identifying a competitor across Play! Pokemon events, required to take part and quoted on reports.
The season-long score awarded by qualifying events, which decides invitations and who may compete for them.
A round a competitor sits out, counted as a win but kept out of tiebreakers.
Order competitors for a bracket by standing or at random, which then decides pairings and who receives byes.
The single-elimination stage that follows the Swiss rounds, and the number of competitors who reach it.
The age band a competitor plays in, fixed for the season by birth year: Junior, Senior or Masters.
A large Championship Series event tier, above which badged entry, stricter reporting and tighter time-extension caps apply.
The office responsible for running an event, reporting Warnings and deciding matters such as re-entry.
The event's Organizer, Judges, Scorekeepers and casters taken together, who may ask to see a competitor's badge and to whom lying is an infraction.
